# Northern Cancer Registry

## Summary

The population-based cancer registry for the region served by the institute and its partner hospitals. Through the [[registry-linkage-agreement]] it is the source of cancer incidence and death follow-up for the Northvale Health Cohort and of recurrence-related deaths and second primaries for the St Aldric MRD patients. [[daniel-asante]] is our working contact on the registry side.

## Why It Matters

Every outcome in the [[northvale-early-detection-study]] and the [[ch-cancer-risk-analysis]] comes from this registry, and so does vital status for the [[pancreatic-cfdna-mrd-study]]. Its lag and its rules on onward transfer decide what we can analyse and when, and the onward transfer rule is now one of the two open points in the [[data-access-policy-revision]].

## Key Details

- Linkage scope: consented Northvale participants (86,400) and St Aldric MRD patients (212). Identifiers sent: national ID, date of birth, sex, postcode sector. The registry links in-house and returns a pseudonymised extract keyed by study ID.
- Variables returned: ICD-O-3 topography and morphology, date of diagnosis, basis of diagnosis, stage at diagnosis where recorded (about 70% complete for pancreatic and colorectal cancer since 2015), vital status, date and underlying cause of death. No treatment data.
- Lag: about 95% of a calendar year's cases are registered twelve months after year end and above 99% after 24 months (figures from [[daniel-asante]]). The 2025 extract received on 2026-09-08 is therefore provisional for 2025 diagnoses.
- Death data comes from the registry's mortality feed, usually more current than incidence by about three months.
- Match rate in the 2025 extract for the [[registry-linkage-update]]: 99.2% of the 86,400 Northvale participants on the deterministic key, most of the rest resolved by the registry's probabilistic step.
- Refresh: up to two per year under the agreement; target delivery within three months of request.

## Caveats

Stage is missing often enough that stage-specific lead-time estimates need a missing-data sensitivity analysis. Recurrence itself is not registered; for the MRD study recurrence still comes from St Aldric clinical records, the registry only adds deaths and new primaries. Registry-derived variables may not leave the institute without the registry's written consent.

## Source Location

Extracts land in the institute secure data environment under `linkage/northern-cancer-registry/` (root key `corvane_sde`), one folder per delivery. The agreement itself is summarised in [[registry-linkage-agreement-summary]].
